findings.summary: Existing markdown-folder and vault-boundary tests already cover isolated capture, change, tombstone, paging exhaust, and subject stability. They do not independently specify selected-folder isolation from sibling/parent files, a mixed unchanged/changed/deleted resume on a new connector instance, non-repetition of that mixed resume, fresh backfill after deletion (current files only), or identical-text distinct identities.

expectations: Selecting an independent synthetic folder captures only that folder's ordinary markdown (relative ids and texts); parent and sibling files are not ingested.
Repeat backfill(null) of an unchanged selected folder re-emits the same source_record_id and subjects.
sync(cursor) of an unchanged selected folder emits no events.

One resume after editing one ordinary file and deleting another emits the new text for the edited id (same subjects) and a tombstone for the deleted id (same subjects), and does not re-emit the unchanged file.
A further resume does not repeat the change or tombstone.
A fresh backfill(null) after deletion reports the current files only and does not emit a historical tombstone.
Two ordinary files with identical text keep distinct, stable source_record_id and subject identities; an idle resume emits nothing.
